title: Cascadia Health: fourteen clinic websites merged into one
answerBlock: Cascadia Health, a healthcare provider in Oregon, was running fourteen separate clinic websites. We merged them into one accessible WordPress platform with location-aware appointment booking, verified against WCAG 2.2 AA. Online bookings rose 91% and the team now maintains one site instead of fourteen.
summary: Fourteen clinic sites merged into one accessible platform with location-aware appointment booking.

seo.title: Cascadia Health: multi-clinic website case study
seo.description: How Cascadia Health merged fourteen clinic websites into one accessible WordPress platform with location-aware booking: online bookings up 91%.

cover.alt: Hands typing on a laptop beside a stethoscope

challenge: Each of Cascadia Health's fourteen clinics had a website of its own. That meant fourteen places to update, and a patient looking for an appointment had to find the right clinic's site before they could book.
Small changes were slow. Staff could not publish their own updates, so something as simple as a new phone number waited on someone else to make it.
approach: We brought the fourteen clinics onto one platform instead of redesigning fourteen sites. Every clinic is a location within one website, so there is one design, one set of templates and one place to maintain.
Accessibility was a requirement from the first design rather than an audit at the end, because a healthcare website has to work for every patient who needs it.
build: The platform runs on WordPress, so Cascadia's own staff publish their updates without a developer.
Appointment booking is location-aware: a patient books with the clinic that suits them from one website. The platform is verified against WCAG 2.2 at level AA.

gallery.alt: The reception desk of a bright, modern clinic lobby
A clinician in a white coat talking with a patient
A clinician in a white coat holding a smartphone

outcome: Online bookings rose 91% after the clinics moved onto one platform. Fourteen sites became one to maintain, and staff publish their own updates instead of waiting for a change to be made for them.
measurement: Commercial figures come from the client's own analytics, twelve months after launch, and every figure is one the client agreed to publish. Speed and accessibility results, such as load times, Lighthouse scores and WCAG conformance, are measured on the live site.

quote.quote: Fourteen clinic websites became one. Our staff publish their own updates now, which sounds small until you remember we used to wait nine days for a phone number change.
